questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am very busy now."
options: He said that he is very busy now.
He said that he was very busy then.
He said that I was very busy then.
He says that he was very busy now.
questions.explanation: In indirect speech the present tense shifts to past and 'now' becomes 'then'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Where do you live?"
options: She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I lived.
She said me where I lived.
She asked me where do I live.
questions.explanation: A reported question drops the auxiliary and takes statement order: where I lived.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "The earth moves round the sun."
options: The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher told that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said the earth is moving round the sun.
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps its present tense even after a past reporting verb.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Please help me."
options: He requested me to help him.
He said me to help him.
He ordered me to help him.
He asked me that I help him.
questions.explanation: 'Please' signals a request, so the reporting verb becomes 'requested' with a to-infinitive.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "What a beautiful bird it is!"
options: He said that what a beautiful bird it was.
He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful bird.
He asked what a beautiful bird it was.
He exclaimed what a beautiful bird it is.
questions.explanation: An exclamatory sentence becomes assertive with 'exclaimed that' and an intensifier such as 'very'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I shall go tomorrow."
options: He said that he shall go tomorrow.
He said that he would go the next day.
He said that he will go the next day.
He said that he would go tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Shall' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.stem: Change into passive voice: 'They are building a house.'
options: A house is building by them.
A house is being built by them.
A house has been built by them.
A house was being built by them.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active becomes 'is/are being + past participle' in the passive.

questions.stem: Change into passive voice: 'Open the door.'
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes passive with 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive voice: 'I know him.'
options: He has been known by me.
questions.explanation: Verbs of knowing take 'to' rather than 'by' in the passive: he is known TO me.

questions.stem: Change into passive voice: 'He writes a letter.'
options: A letter is written by him.
A letter was written by him.
A letter is being written by him.
A letter has written by him.
questions.explanation: Simple present active becomes 'is/are + past participle' in the passive.

questions.stem: Change into active voice: 'The work has been finished by them.'
questions.explanation: 'Has been + past participle' corresponds to the present perfect active: they HAVE finished.

questions.stem: Change into passive voice: 'She sang a song.'
options: A song is sung by her.
A song was sung by her.
A song was sang by her.
A song had sung by her.
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle'. The participle of 'sing' is 'sung'.

questions.stem: ‘বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: এখন ঘটছে এমন কাজ বোঝাতে present continuous ব্যবহৃত হয় — It is raining.

questions.stem: ‘আমরা কাজটি শেষ করেছি’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: সদ্য সম্পন্ন কাজ বোঝাতে present perfect — We have finished.

questions.stem: ‘লোকটি তিন দিন ধরে জ্বরে ভুগছে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: The man suffers from fever for three days.
The man is suffering from fever for three days.
The man has been suffering from fever for three days.
The man suffered from fever three days.
questions.explanation: ‘ধরে’ অর্থাৎ কাজটি চলছে — present perfect continuous with 'for three days'.

questions.stem: ‘সে ভাত খায় না’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: তৃতীয় পুরুষ একবচনে simple present-এর নেতিবাচক রূপ 'does not + verb'.

questions.stem: ‘তুমি কি ইংরেজি জানো?’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: Simple present-এর প্রশ্নবোধক রূপ 'Do + subject + verb'.

questions.stem: ‘সে গতকাল ঢাকা গিয়েছিল’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: He has gone to Dhaka yesterday.
He was going to Dhaka yesterday.
questions.explanation: ‘গতকাল’ নির্দিষ্ট অতীত সময় — simple past 'went'.

questions.stem: He is good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: 'Good at' is used for skill in a subject or activity.

questions.stem: She was married ___ a doctor.
questions.explanation: One is married TO a person, though married BY the person who conducts the ceremony.

questions.stem: He is senior ___ me by two years.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives — senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior — take 'to', never 'than'.

questions.stem: I congratulated him ___ his success.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate somebody ON something' is the fixed collocation.

questions.stem: He died ___ cholera.
questions.explanation: 'Die of' is used with a disease; 'die from' with a cause such as an injury.

questions.stem: The book is ___ the table.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used for a surface contact.

questions.stem: By next December he ___ his degree.
questions.explanation: An action finished before a future point takes the future perfect: will have completed.

questions.stem: She ___ to school when I saw her.
questions.explanation: An action in progress when another past action interrupted it takes the past continuous.

questions.stem: It is a long time since we ___.
questions.explanation: After 'It is a long time since', the verb takes the simple past.

questions.stem: If it rains, we ___ at home.
questions.explanation: First conditional: 'if + simple present' is completed by 'will + base verb'.

questions.stem: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact takes the simple present, with -s for a singular subject.

questions.stem: I ___ him at the market yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' fixes a definite past time, so the simple past 'saw' is required.
